rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-one builder trees go (a row of ficus, corals, magnolias and jacarandas along the back fences, two 3 m from the house fronts, others in the yards); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the grills and chairs, the swing set, and the open lot corner inside the wrought-iron fence.

trees.why: the back yard with the kettle grill and the white adirondack: a coral tree over both
the yard across the back line with its own grill and adirondack, 37 m on: the same shade for the neighbours
the back yard with the swing set (2.6 m off): shade over the swings
the open lot corner inside the wrought-iron fence, 43 m from the walls: a full magnolia
the north yard inside the same fence, 13 m from the house: a jacaranda, 32 m from the magnolia
